name: Deepak Nitrite Ltd
about: Incorporated in 1970, Deepak Nitrite Ltd manufactures Basic Intermediates, Fine & Speciality Chemicals, Performance Products, and Phenolics [1]

statements.text: Revenue compounded 12.6% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax -6.6%.
EBITDA margin compressed 1620 bps over 5 years (28.7% → 12.5%).
Revenue growth accelerated from 4% to 62% YoY over the last 4 quarters.
Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 20.4%, 970 bps above a year ago.
Over 5 years: ₹3,978 cr of profit, ₹3,512 cr of operating cash — conversion 0.88x, adequate.

flags.text: Large capex underway: CWIP ₹1,299 cr = 31% of fixed assets

ledger.quote: we should be targeting something along the lines of about 14% to 15% EBIT
ledger.statement: Steady-state EBIT margin target of 14-15% next year, once commissioned assets run at steady state
ledger.speaker: Maulik Mehta
ledger.evidence: FY28 target given in Q2 FY27; FY28 has not started. The quote says EBIT but the ledger tags it as ebitda_margin, and the segment it applies to is not stated. Group margin is already 20.4% (F:margin_last_q_pct) and Phenolics EBIT is about 22% (C2), so the 14-15% EBIT most likely refers to a segment or the new assets.

ledger.quote: it would be roughly in the range of about INR 400 crore, INR 420 crore
ledger.statement: Incremental EBIT of INR 400-420 crore next year from existing assets
ledger.speaker: Maulik Mehta
ledger.evidence: FY28 incremental EBIT of INR 400-420 crore from existing assets (C3). Period not started; C3 also frames it as 'INR 250 crore plus another INR 250 crore' of steady-state visibility, which is not the same number.

ledger.quote: there, I would expect about another INR 240 crore is what we're seeing this year
ledger.statement: Incremental EBIT of about INR 240 crore this year from full asset utilization
ledger.speaker: Maulik Mehta
ledger.evidence: Said in Q2 FY27 for FY27 (ends March 2027). There is no later call. C7 guides Q3 EBIT margin between Q1 and Q2 and closer to Q1, with absolute gains from DCTL assets landing in Q3-Q4, so most of the INR 240 crore is back-end loaded.

ledger.quote: INR 2,200 crore-INR 2,400 crore next year, INR 2,500 crore in the second year
ledger.statement: Planned investment of INR 2,200-2,400 crore in FY28, then INR 2,500 crore in FY29 (per passage context)
ledger.speaker: Sanjay Upadhyay
ledger.evidence: FY28 capex guidance, period not started. This is itself a downward revision from INR 3,000 crore (G14) and moves INR 2,500 crore into the following year, i.e. spend is being re-phased later.

ledger.quote: we continue to remain in line with our FY29 number
ledger.statement: Remain in line with FY29 number for integrated propylene-to-polycarbonate commissioning
ledger.speaker: Maulik Mehta
ledger.evidence: FY29 milestone reiterated in Q2 FY27. No independent progress data in the inputs, and the earlier H2 polycarbonate wording (G10) muddies which date is the real one.

ledger.quote: in FY31, you already have seen a fully optimized utilization of polycarbonate
ledger.statement: Polycarbonate capacity fully utilised by FY31 after upstream integration
ledger.speaker: Maulik Mehta
ledger.evidence: FY31 horizon. Depends on FY29 upstream integration (G5), and there is no progress data.

ledger.quote: we will be able to add another 80 to 100 KTPA in the market from the new capacity
ledger.statement: Add 80-100 KTPA of market supply from new capacity
ledger.speaker: Maulik Mehta
ledger.evidence: No horizon given, and the inputs contain no capacity or volume data to test 80-100 KTPA of additional market supply.

ledger.quote: So I would assume that in Q4 EBIT percentage should be better than Q3.
ledger.statement: Q4FY27 EBIT margin to be better than Q3FY27
ledger.speaker: Maulik Mehta
ledger.evidence: Q3 and Q4 FY27 not yet reported. C7 sets a lower Q3 base ('closer to Q1') that Q4 would need to beat.

ledger.quote: MIBK as well as MIBC will be commissioned along with acetophenone in August itself, and the rest of them will be commissioned within Q2.
ledger.statement: MIBK, MIBC and acetophenone projects commissioned in August 2026, remaining projects within Q2FY27
ledger.speaker: Maulik Mehta
ledger.evidence: The Q2 FY27 call says MIBK and MIBC assets 'have also been commissioned' (C8), and the DCTL chlorination, photochlorination, hydrogenation and fluorination plants were commissioned by end-Q2 (C3, C5). The August date and acetophenone are not specifically confirmed, and C5 says MIBK/MIBC are still in commercialisation and scale-up.
ledger.actual_text: MIBK/MIBC and DCTL plants commissioned within Q2 FY27 (C3, C5, C8)

ledger.quote: I would anticipate that we would target H2 for our polycarbonate commissioning.
ledger.statement: Polycarbonate project commissioning targeted for H2FY27
ledger.speaker: Maulik Mehta
ledger.evidence: Q1 FY27 targeted 'H2' for polycarbonate commissioning (tagged H2 FY27). The Q2 FY27 call anchors integrated propylene-to-polycarbonate to FY29 (G5) and full utilisation to FY31 (G6), and no passage mentions a start-up in H2 FY27. Either the horizon was mis-tagged (H2 of a later year) or the date has moved by more than a year.

ledger.quote: we are going to make, I think, about some INR 70-odd crore investment further in debottlenecking the assets to be able to touch about 4 lakh tonnes
ledger.statement: About INR70 crore debottlenecking investment to reach about 4 lakh tonnes
ledger.speaker: Maulik Mehta
ledger.evidence: No horizon given, and no later call or context reports on the INR 70 crore debottlenecking or progress toward 4 lakh tonnes.

ledger.quote: Further this year, we'll spend around another INR 1,000 crore to INR 1,500 crore this year further.
ledger.statement: Capex of INR1,000-1,500 crore in FY27 (conflicts with the INR1,500-1,600 crore figure given later)
ledger.speaker: Sanjay Upadhyay
ledger.evidence: FY27 not over. It conflicts with G13 from the same Q1 FY27 call (INR 1,500-1,600 crore), and both undercut the INR 2,500 crore given in Q3 FY26 (G25).

ledger.quote: Further, this year, it will be around INR 1,500 crore to INR 1,600 crore.
ledger.statement: Capex of INR1,500-1,600 crore in FY27
ledger.speaker: Sanjay Upadhyay
ledger.evidence: FY27 not over and no capex actual in the facts. The same Q1 FY27 call also gave INR 1,000-1,500 crore (G12), and both are well below the INR 2,500 crore FY27 figure given in Q3 FY26 (G25). The Q2 FY27 inputs do not update the FY27 capex number.

ledger.quote: whatever we are going to spend in 2027, 2028 will be another INR 3,000 crore
ledger.statement: Capex of about INR3,000 crore in FY27-FY28 beyond the projects already funded
ledger.speaker: Sanjay Upadhyay
ledger.evidence: Drift record: the FY28 capex of INR 3,000 crore (Q1 FY27) was cut to INR 2,200-2,400 crore in Q2 FY27 (G4), 20-27% lower, with INR 2,500 crore now placed in the following year. Caveat: the ledger statement reads this as an FY27-FY28 figure. If it was a two-year total, then G13 plus G4 (INR 3,700-4,000 crore) would be a raise, not a cut, so the basis is ambiguous.
ledger.actual_text: FY28 capex now guided at INR 2,200-2,400 crore (G4)

ledger.quote: But debt-to-equity ratio will be very, very comfortable. It will not cross even 1.
ledger.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio to stay at or below 1x
ledger.speaker: Sanjay Upadhyay
ledger.evidence: Debt-to-equity is 0.27x (F:debt_to_equity) on borrowings of INR 1,762 crore (F:borrowings_cr). The test is ahead: the INR 11,000 crore project funded 60:40 implies about INR 6,600 crore of debt (G20), about 3.7x current borrowings.

ledger.quote: we should be able to ramp up to beyond 100% very quickly
ledger.statement: Ramp utilisation beyond 100% quickly as demand comes in
ledger.speaker: Maulik Mehta
ledger.evidence: No horizon given, and the asset is not identified. The only utilisation datapoint is IPA 'by and large' at 100% (C8), and nitric acid is still ramping (C5).

ledger.quote: MIBK, MIBC projects, which are scheduled for commissioning in Q2 FY27
ledger.statement: MIBK and MIBC projects scheduled for commissioning in Q2FY27
ledger.speaker: Maulik Mehta
ledger.evidence: The Q2 FY27 call confirms the MIBK and MIBC assets are commissioned (C8) and in commercialisation and scale-up (C5), within the Q2 FY27 window.

ledger.quote: maybe perhaps at the tail end of Q1 or the early part of Q2 is when we will be looking at commissioning of the asset
ledger.statement: Commissioning of the new plant asset around end-Q1 to early-Q2FY27, after mechanical completion
ledger.speaker: Maulik Mehta

ledger.quote: Therefore, in FY27, we expect a stronger margin profile, even for the standalone business, compared with FY26.
ledger.statement: Stronger margin profile for the standalone business in FY27 versus FY26
ledger.speaker: Maulik Mehta

ledger.quote: the total project, what we have announced is around INR11,000 crore
ledger.statement: Total announced project size of about INR11,000 crore, funded 60:40 debt to equity
ledger.speaker: Sanjay Upadhyay
ledger.evidence: Project size and 60:40 funding is a multi-year plan. Phased capex of INR 2,200-2,400 crore in FY28 and INR 2,500 crore in FY29 (G4) is consistent with it, but no spend-to-date figure is in the inputs.

ledger.quote: Q4 FY26 will be better, but Q1 FY27 will be better still.
ledger.statement: Performance to improve in Q4FY26 vs Q3FY26 and further in Q1FY27
ledger.speaker: Maulik Mehta

ledger.quote: we are expecting to run at 100% or close enough to 100% utilization from this quarter onwards
ledger.statement: Run nitration, hydrogenation and nitric acid assets at about 100% utilisation from Q4FY26
ledger.speaker: Maulik Mehta
ledger.evidence: The target was about 100% utilisation of nitration, hydrogenation and nitric acid from Q4 FY26. In Q2 FY27 management was still 'continuing with the ramp-up' of the nitric acid facility (C5) and put the remaining upside from 'full asset utilization... including nitration and nitric acid' at about INR 240 crore this year (C3), so full utilisation had not been reached two quarters later.
ledger.actual_text: Nitric acid still ramping in Q2 FY27 (C3, C5)

ledger.quote: When we talk about MIBK, it will have a ramp-up in Q1 FY27 in a phased manner
ledger.statement: MIBK capacity to ramp up in Q1FY27 in phases
ledger.speaker: Maulik Mehta
ledger.evidence: Q3 FY26 guided MIBK ramp-up in Q1 FY27. The Q1 FY27 call moved MIBK commissioning to August (G9), and it was confirmed commissioned only on the Q2 FY27 call (C8). It slipped by about one quarter.
ledger.actual_text: Commissioned in Q2 FY27, one quarter late (G9, C8)

ledger.quote: which will come in around between June and July 2026
ledger.statement: High-pressure alkylation asset to come online June-July 2026, completing Phase 1 of investments
ledger.speaker: Maulik Mehta
ledger.evidence: The June-July 2026 window has passed, but no later call or context mentions the high-pressure alkylation asset or completion of Phase 1. The Q2 FY27 commissioning list (C3) covers nitric acid, chlorination, photochlorination, hydrogenation and fluorination only.

ledger.quote: INR 2,500 crore is for FY27, not FY26.
ledger.statement: Capex of about INR 2,500 crore planned for FY27
ledger.speaker: Sanjay Upadhyay
ledger.evidence: Q3 FY26 put FY27 capex at about INR 2,500 crore. By Q1 FY27 the guidance was INR 1,000-1,500 crore (G12) or INR 1,500-1,600 crore (G13), 36-60% lower. Both Q1 quotes say 'further/another', so spend already made in Q1 may sit on top. This pair is not in the drift list, so the cut is partly a basis question.
ledger.actual_text: FY27 capex re-guided to INR 1,000-1,600 crore 'further' (G12, G13)

ledger.quote: bringing the total to approximately INR 1,200–1,300 crore
ledger.statement: Total capex of about INR 1,200-1,300 crore in FY26
ledger.speaker: Sanjay Upadhyay
ledger.evidence: FY26 has ended, but the facts do not include an FY26 capex figure, so the INR 1,200-1,300 crore cannot be tested. F:fcf_5y_cr of INR -139 crore only shows capex absorbed operating cash over five years.

ledger.quote: this will come online in Q1 FY27
ledger.statement: BTC to BTF (or equivalent) product capacity online in Q1FY27
ledger.speaker: Maulik Mehta
ledger.evidence: Q1 FY27 has ended, but no passage dates BTC/BTF output. C3 lists photochlorination and fluorination as commissioned by the Q2 call, while C5 says DCTL chlorination came only 'towards the end of' Q2, which hints at slippage without proving it.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management calls Q2 a record quarter and says it is confident of steady-state EBIT and of the new capacity ramp-up, while noting sequential margin moderation from input prices and freight.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management reports record EBITDA and says it remains very confident in delivering growth profitably, while acknowledging delays in pre-commissioning and feedstock volatility.

tones.label: confident
tones.why: Management says "We are also working towards a return to what we consider normalcy a couple of years ago" and expects the new downstream products to be margin accretive.

tones.label: cautious
tones.why: Management says it is cautiously optimistic and calls the coming quarter volatile and hard to predict, while expecting gradual improvement from Q4FY26.

context.speaker: Maulik Mehta
context.text: Thank you. Good afternoon everybody, and a warm welcome to Deepak Nitrite's Q2 & H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call. Thank you for your continued interest in the Company. Our investor presentation and financial results have already been shared, and I trust you had an opportunity to review them. I will begin by sharing our perspective on the operating environment, business performance and strategic developments, following which Mr. Upadhyay will take you through the financial results in greater detail. At the outset, I am delighted to announce that we have achieved the Best Ever Performance in Deepak Nitrite's operating history of over 5 decades, delivering record Revenue and EBITDA on both a quarterly as well as a half yearly basis. Consolidated revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 stood at INR 3,091 crore, registering a sequential growth of 19% and year-on-year growth of 61%. What makes this achievement particularly noteworthy is the challenging environment in which it has been accomplished. I would like to congratulate our entire team for its commitment, agility and outstanding execution. The global chemical industry continues to navigate significant volatility arising from geopolitical developments, disruptions to international trade, elevated freight and energy costs as well as uneven demand across end-use applications. These developments are also influencing sourcing preferences, with customers increasingly valuing assured delivery, consistent quality as well as reliability of supply. Page 2 of 20 Deepak Nitrite Limited October 30, 2026 For Deepak, this environment has presented opportunities as well as challenges. context.speaker: Sanjay Upadhyay
context.text: Thank you, Maulik, and good afternoon everyone. I'll take you through the financial and segmental performance for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026, followed by an update on our balance sheet and capital allocation. Financial performance for Q2 marked another record quarter for Deepak Group. Consolidated revenue from operations increased to INR 3,091 crore, registering growth of 61% year-on-year and 19% sequentially. EBITDA reached a record INR 643 crore, growing at 187% year-on-year and 16% quarter-on-quarter with EBITDA margin sustained at 21%. Page 4 of 20 Deepak Nitrite Limited October 30, 2026 PBT increased to INR 543 crore, while PAT reached INR 398 crore, representing sequential growth of 16% and 15%, respectively. For H1 FY27, consolidated revenue stood at INR 5,682 crore registering 48% year-on-year growth. EBITDA increased 173% to INR 1,197 crore with margins expanding to 21% compared with approximately 11% in corresponding period last year. PAT increased 221% to INR 743 crore. The significant year-on-year improvement reflects higher operational throughput, favorable product economics, effective procurement and better utilization of our manufacturing assets. Now on segmental performance. Phenolics delivered highest ever quarterly revenue of INR 2,291 crore, an increase of 29% sequentially and 72% year-on-year. EBIT increased to INR 515 crore, up 23% quarter-on-quarter, with EBIT margin of approximately 22%. For H1 FY27, the segment recorded revenue of INR 4,066 crore and EBIT of INR 933 crore. I am sure many of you would have noticed that in just the first 6 months of this financial year, our EBIT of INR 933 crore has surpassed previous highest annual EBIT of INR 867 crore, which was registered in FY22. context.speaker: Maulik Mehta
context.text: Okay. So Sanjesh, the nitric acid plant has been commissioned, the chlorination, photochlorination, hydrogenation, fluorination, all of these plants have also been commissioned. With regards to absolute EBIT, those are conversations that we are having with certain customers for new applications where these are contractual in nature. We're confident of being able to have a significant market share. And what you're asking about is with regards to full asset utilization of all our assets, including nitration and nitric acid. So there, I would expect about another INR 240 crore is what we're seeing this year. And if I was to look at next year, it would be roughly in the range of about INR 400 crore, INR 420 crore. There is an upside available. So we can assume that INR 250 crore plus another INR 250 crore is the kind of visibility that we have on steady state for the existed investments.

Growth will be supported by an improvement in the demand across various product categories, capacity-led expansion in select product lines and the gradual ramp-up of recently commissioned facility. We're also continuing to diversify our product portfolio, customer base as well as geographic presence. This approach is intended to reduce dependence on individual products or markets, improve our ability to serve customers and create a more resilient earnings base.

During the quarter, we continued with the ramp-up of recently commissioned assets including the nitric acid facility, while progressing with the commercialization as well as scale up for manufacturing downstream products such as MIBK, MIBC as well as the derivatives. Page 3 of 20 Deepak Nitrite Limited October 30, 2026 Moreover, towards the end of the quarter, Deepak Chemtech also commissioned its chlorination, which is in addition to the photohalogenation assets as well as specialty chemicals plant in Dahej with capital investment of approximately INR 300 crore, including associated utilities and infra.

Looking ahead, we remain encouraged by the opportunities across businesses. In Phenolics, our priority is to sustain high throughput, strengthen downstream value addition and grow wallet share. Within Advanced Intermediates, improving capacity utilization, new product introductions and the ongoing recovery in deferred demand provide additional avenues for growth. As our new assets progressively ramp up and customer qualifications translate into commercial volumes, we expect an increasingly diversified contribution from our portfolio.

Okay. So we expect Q3, in terms of EBIT percentage, somewhere between Q1 and Q2, I think closer to Q1 in terms of percentage. In terms of absolute, we expect to have numbers which, including the addition of the assets which are commissioned in DCTL add substantially from Q3 and Q4 onwards. So I would assume that in Q4 EBIT percentage should be better than Q3. And on an annualized basis from next year onwards, we should see further improvement. Some of these investments that we have commissioned, especially in agchem, they are linked to annualized procurement contracts that are there with customers.

So any disturbance in propylene supply is something that would possibly affect other manufacturers more than Deepak Nitrite. There, we do have this benefit. By and large, we've run IPA at 100%. But for us, we always focus on the integrated value. So if we find that acetone is able to drive more value, IPA is able to drive more value, and now we've also commissioned our MIBK and MIBC assets. So all put together, we are approaching the business via an integrated platform play.

Okay. So Sanjesh, the nitric acid plant has been commissioned, the chlorination, photochlorination, hydrogenation, fluorination, all of these plants have also been commissioned. With regards to absolute EBIT, those are conversations that we are having with certain customers for new applications where these are contractual in nature. We're confident of being able to have a significant market share. And what you're asking about is with regards to full asset utilization of all our assets, including nitration and nitric acid. So there, I would expect about another INR 240 crore is what we're seeing this year.

business.what_it_does: Indian chemicals producer running an integrated Phenolics chain (phenol/acetone, IPA, and newly commissioned MIBK/MIBC downstream) alongside an Advanced Intermediates business (nitric acid, nitration, hydrogenation), with a subsidiary, Deepak Chemtech (DCTL), that commissioned chlorination, photohalogenation, fluorination and specialty-chemical assets at Dahej (about INR 300 crore) and an announced INR 11,000 crore propylene-to-polycarbonate project. Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue was INR 3,091 crore.

segments.name: Phenolics
segments.comment: Q2 FY27 revenue INR 2,291 crore of INR 3,091 crore consolidated (computed share, before inter-segment eliminations); +72% YoY, +29% QoQ; EBIT INR 515 crore at about 22% margin.

segments.name: Advanced Intermediates
segments.comment: Revenue not stated in the inputs; management cites utilisation gains, new products and recovery in deferred demand. Includes the nitric acid and nitration assets still ramping.

segments.name: Deepak Chemtech (DCTL) new assets
segments.comment: Chlorination, photohalogenation, fluorination and specialty-chemical plants commissioned around end-Q2 FY27; agchem volumes tied to annual contracts; no revenue yet disclosed.

H1 FY27 revenue and margin delivery was strong.

narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Reported numbers match: revenue +61.7% YoY, operating margin 20.4% vs 10.7% in the same quarter last year, PAT +234.5% YoY.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: The record quarter marks a structural step-up from higher throughput, product economics and better asset utilisation (C2, C6).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: The record is in rupees, not in profitability or multi-year growth. Revenue CAGR is -0.4% over three years, PAT CAGR is -13.5% over three years and -6.6% over five, and the margin is 370 bps lower than three years ago and 1,620 bps lower than five years ago. Two of the last four quarters had revenue growth of 3.8% and -2.8%.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Newly commissioned assets will add about INR 240 crore of EBIT in FY27 and INR 400-420 crore in FY28 (G3, G2), with Q4 margins above Q3 (G8).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: None of this is in reported numbers yet. Management itself guides Q3 EBIT margin down toward Q1 levels (C7), the earlier full-utilisation date was missed (G22), and ROCE is 11.0% on the asset base built so far.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Balance sheet stays 'very, very comfortable', with debt-to-equity not crossing 1x while funding an INR 11,000 crore project 60:40 (G15, G20).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Leverage is low today at 0.27x D/E and INR 1,762 crore borrowings. Cash generation is weak, though: five-year FCF is INR -139 crore, CFO/PAT is 0.88 and the cash conversion cycle has lengthened from 76 to 92 days. The roughly INR 6,600 crore of project debt implied by 60:40 will have to be borrowed rather than funded internally.

bull.point: Earnings inflection is in reported numbers: Q2 FY27 revenue +61.7% YoY, operating margin 20.4% vs 10.7% a year earlier, TTM PAT INR 1,063 crore on TTM revenue of INR 9,749 crore.

The new asset pipeline is now commissioned: MIBK/MIBC plus DCTL chlorination, photochlorination, hydrogenation and fluorination (C3, C5, C8). Management quantifies INR 240 crore of incremental EBIT for FY27 and INR 400-420 crore for FY28, against H1 FY27 EBITDA of INR 1,197 crore. Agchem volumes are tied to annual contracts (C7).
There is room to borrow for the polycarbonate build. D/E is 0.27x against a self-set 1x ceiling, and borrowings are INR 1,762 crore against a project plan that implies about INR 6,600 crore of debt.

bear.point: Project dates slip. About 100% utilisation of nitric acid and nitration was promised from Q4 FY26, but those assets were still ramping in Q2 FY27, with INR 240 crore of upside still to come. MIBK was guided for Q1 FY27 and commissioned in Q2.

Capex and project timelines keep moving. FY27 capex went from INR 2,500 crore to INR 1,000-1,500 crore and INR 1,500-1,600 crore in the same call. FY28 capex went from INR 3,000 crore to INR 2,200-2,400 crore, with INR 2,500 crore pushed into the next year. Polycarbonate went from 'H2' to FY29, with full utilisation in FY31.

Returns and cash conversion are thin ahead of a 60%-debt-funded INR 11,000 crore project. ROCE is 11.0%, five-year FCF is INR -139 crore, CFO/PAT is 0.88 and the cash cycle has stretched from 76 to 92 days. Management also guides the Q3 EBIT margin back toward Q1 levels.

questions: Q1 FY27 said 'H2' for polycarbonate commissioning; Q2 FY27 says integrated commissioning in FY29 and full utilisation in FY31. Which is the committed date for first polycarbonate output, and what changed between the two calls?

Nitric acid and nitration were meant to run at about 100% from Q4 FY26. What utilisation did they actually run at in Q2 FY27, and how much of the INR 240 crore FY27 and INR 400-420 crore FY28 EBIT bridge is volume versus assumed spreads?

Reconcile the capex numbers: INR 2,500 crore for FY27 (Q3 FY26) against INR 1,000-1,500 crore and INR 1,500-1,600 crore (Q1 FY27), and INR 3,000 crore against INR 2,200-2,400 crore for FY28. Also, what drove the cash conversion cycle from 76 to 92 days while revenue grew 61.7%?
